description: A three-panel figure of secondary-electron SEM micrographs of Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steel after treatment at 600 °C; the caption letter-labels only (a) and (b). All three panels carry identical in-image metadata: "20kV", "X10,000" and a "1µm" scale bar. (a) 9Al-10Mn-0.4C: a colony of fine, closely spaced bright lamellae/rods nucleates on an almost straight boundary decorated with small bright particles and grows into one grain, while the adjacent region remains smooth and dark (unreacted austenite). (b) 9Al-10Mn-1C: lamellar colonies fill most of the field, fans of parallel lamellae impinging on one another at colony boundaries, with only a dark unreacted patch at the top — i.e. the discontinuous reaction has consumed most of the austenite. The bottom panel (panel letter cropped, black borders) shows a coarser morphology of angular blocky and plate-like bright particles in a dark matrix, unlike the fine lamellae of (a) and (b); its attribution is unclear. Taken together, the panels support the argument that raising C from 0.4 to 1 wt.% drives the γ → γ + κ-carbide discontinuous precipitation from a grain-boundary-initiated reaction to near-complete austenite transformation, both producing fine γ + κ-carbide lamellae. No numeric property values are printed on any panel.

observations.observation: All three panels are SEM micrographs sharing identical in-image metadata printed at the lower edge: '20kV', 'X10,000' and a '1µm' scale bar.

Panel (a) shows a single colony of fine, closely spaced bright lamellae/rods nucleating on a nearly straight boundary that is decorated with small bright particles, growing into a darker grain while the adjacent area stays smooth and dark.

Panel (b) shows lamellar colonies covering most of the field of view, with fans of parallel bright lamellae impinging on one another at colony boundaries and a dark unreacted region remaining only at the top.

The third (bottom) panel shows coarse angular blocky and plate-like bright particles in a dark matrix, a morphology clearly different from the fine lamellae of (a) and (b); the panel is cropped with black bars and bears no legible panel letter.
The caption states that the figure shows discontinuous precipitation in γ + κ-carbide lamellae at 600 °C in (a) 9Al-10Mn-0.4C and (b) 9Al-10Mn-1C.
The caption names only two panels, (a) and (b), so the third supplied micrograph is not accounted for by the caption.
The citing text asserts that in 9Al-10Mn-0.4C discontinuous precipitation starts from the grain boundaries (Fig. 2(a)).
The citing text asserts that in 9Al-10Mn-1C most of the austenite is transformed through the discontinuous precipitation reaction (Fig. 2(b)).
The citing text asserts that in both alloys γ + κ-carbide fine lamellae were produced.

The citing text states that in 9Al-10Mn-1C the non-discontinuous precipitated austenite appears to have featured nano-sized κ-carbide precipitation, as suggested by EDS (Table 3) — a feature not resolvable at the ×10,000 magnification shown here.
The citing text states that 9Al-10Mn-1C treated at 600 °C, with fine lamellae featuring short inter-lamellar spacing (Fig. 2(b)), showed significant hardening effects (Table 9).

subfigures.description: Secondary-electron SEM micrograph, 20 kV, ×10,000, 1 µm scale bar. A colony of fine parallel bright lamellae/rods grows from an almost straight boundary (decorated with small bright particles) into a darker grain interior; the lower part of the field is smooth, nearly featureless dark matrix (unreacted austenite).

Secondary-electron SEM micrograph, 20 kV, ×10,000, 1 µm scale bar; panel letter '(b)'. Lamellar discontinuous-precipitation colonies fill most of the field of view; bundles/fans of parallel bright lamellae meet at colony boundaries, and only a dark unreacted region remains at the top of the image.

Secondary-electron SEM micrograph, 20 kV, ×10,000, 1 µm scale bar, cropped with black borders and no legible panel letter. Shows coarse angular blocky and elongated plate-like bright particles in a dark matrix — a markedly coarser morphology than the fine lamellae of (a) and (b). Its relation to the caption (which defines only (a) and (b)) cannot be established from the image.
